timeline.author: Tom de Goede

timeline.body:
We often were experiencing deadlocks after terminating or failing a build that uses multiplex workers. Our cause seems to be an interrupted exception being swallowed during [worker.putRequest](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/360265b2664971b42b8e0da451581a9af5890fc4/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/worker/WorkerSpawnRunner.java#L452) causing [worker.getResponse](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/360265b2664971b42b8e0da451581a9af5890fc4/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/worker/WorkerSpawnRunner.java#L467) to wait indefinitely.

I believe this fixes #10288 but I'm not 100% sure this is the only scenario. The issue is also mentioned at https://docs.bazel.build/versions/2.1.0/multiplex-worker.html in the warning section.

timeline.author: Tom de Goede

timeline.body: A good find, thank you! You should catch the exception in WorkerSpawnRunner.java like it already does IOException, so we give good error messages to the user.

Tom, do you have a reliable way to reproduce this? I've tried running with your patch, but interrupting Bazel just gives `Worker process did not return a WorkResponse`, never the new error message, nor have I seen the deadlock.

What are the specs of the machine you're running on? We've seen some deadlock-like effects on machines with ~100 cores.

@larsrc-google I'll see if I can put together a project that reproduces this. We are running on Windows laptops with i7's. We use our  customized dotnet rules which contains the multiplex worker: https://github.com/AFASResearch/rules_dotnet. Which _new error message_ are you referring to? I can imagine that more core's increases the risk of running into this issue because the window for a single action to be calling putRequest just whilest interrupting is really small. If you look at the code I think it's quite obvious that pretending putRequest succeeded is troublesome when getResponse is called unconditionally. I can also look into creating a test that reproduces the issue.

You're right, the error message is not actually new, it's the `InterruptedException was caught while sending worker request` message I meant. 

A test that reproduces it would be awesome. I'll see if I can reproduce it on a many-core machine.

An update: Your CL caused me to think much deeper about interrupts, and how they interact with the new dynamic execution implementation. Your fix doesn't work as it is, as a) an interrupt during IO would turn up as an InterruptedIoException, and b) an interrupt during IO might leave the worker's stdin corrupted.

I'll be working closely on this, as it intersects several tasks I have scheduled for this quarter. And even I, with 25 years of Java experience, learned new things about interrupts looking into this. I certainly see the problem, but the fix is complicated. I'll see about getting the simpler parts of a fix out early rather than wait for a complete solution.

It's still unclear exactly what causes the hang. Using the --worker_quit_after_build would definitely reduce the risk of problems, I can't offhand think of a way the worker would then still be broken afterwards.

The new dynamic execution implementation is currently guarded behind the --legacy_spawn_scheduler flag. See [Joe's blog posts](https://jmmv.dev/series.html#Bazel%20dynamic%20execution) for details. Turning that on makes cancellation a common event, so we need to handle it well.
@tomdegoede Can you confirm that the fix I submitted actually fixes your problem?
@larsrc-google yes! It looks like the issue has been resolved. Thanks 👍
